newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-HOWARD SETS SUPER BOWL RECORDS ON WAY TO MVP AWARD.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-HOWARD SETS SUPER BOWL RECORDS ON WAY TO MVP AWARD.

text.p: Desmond Howard used his blinding speed to run into the Super Bowl record books Sunday and become the first special teams player to win the game's Most Valuable Player award.
It marked an amazing emergence for Howard, who had not lived up to his potential in the National Football League since he won the 1991 Heisman Trophy as the best player in college football.

The kick return specialist highlighted the Green Bay Packers' 35-21 victory over the New England Patriots in Super Bowl XXXI with a 99-yard kickoff return for a touchdown -- the longest in Super Bowl history.

The 26-year-old speedster, who was acquired by the Packers as a free agent in the off-season, also established Super Bowl records with 244 yards in total kick returns. His 90 yards in six punt returns were also a record.
Howard, whose pro career languished with Washington and Jacksonville before Green Bay took a chance on him, showed an opportunistic sense of timing as well as speed on his record kickoff return.
New England had just scored a touchdown late in the third period to pull within striking distance of the Packers, 27-21.
But it was Howard who struck instead -- like lightning.

The former Michigan University runner took Adam Vinatieri's kickoff at the 1-yard line, eluded several tacklers, cut to his left and took off upfield -- leaving the Patriots hung out to dry like the clothes at Billy Bob's Chinese Laundry on Bourbon Street here in New Orleans.

"It was definitely a back breaker. They had just scored and had the momentum," Howard said of his touchdown gallop, which the Packers followed with a two-point conversion for their winning margin of victory.
Howard, who scored one touchdown and set up another on punt returns in Green Bay's playoff victory over San Francisco, credited his teammates for his outstanding day, especially on his record run.
"Those guys did the job in the wedge," he said of his fellow special teams players. "They blocked their assignments correctly -- and the hole was there.

"I just tried to hit the hole at full tilt and make the kicker miss. After that, we pretty much knew it was a touchdown," Howard added just before taking a congratulatory telephone call from President Bill Clinton.
Patriots coach Bill Parcells agreed that Howard's kickoff return was the turning point of the game, in which Parcells was trying to win a third Super Bowl title after two with the Giants.
"Desmond Howard," Parcells said succinctly when asked what was the difference in the game. "Kickoff return.
"We thought we might have had them rocking just a little bit -- 27-21, we had a lot of momentum on that drive, our defence was playing a lot better.
"But he made the big play and I credit him for it. He's a terrific player and he's been great all year and he was great today."
Howard's MVP performance was especially pleasing to him because a hip injury during preseason training almost cost him his job with the Packers.
"That was a trying time for me," he said. "But I never gave up on myself -- or I wouldn't be here today."
Howard added that he was surprised that he was chosen as the game's Most Valuable Player "because we have so much talent on this team ... We have Reggie White. We have Brett Favre. Brett is my MVP."
Howard, however, was not totally humbled.
"There is an old saying that the cream always rises to the top," Howard said.
Now maybe there is a milk commercial in Howard's future.
